text:
maria: Hey @sam — marketing needs a reproducible bench sweep for the launch webinar (target date Mon 2026-04-06). We want: p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec, per-token cost, and the exact commands/configs so we can include a small methodology blurb in the deck. Can eng/runtime run a smoke by EOD Wed and a full sweep by Fri?

sam: Ack. I can do a smoke tonight and schedule full sweep. Quick clarifying q's: which models and quant variants do you want included? exact sequence length distribution? hardware targets? and do you need raw logs/artifacts or just summarized CSVs + command lines?

maria: Thanks. Priority models: open-model-1 (fp16), open-model-1-quant (int8), and an Llama-compat baseline. Sequence buckets: 128, 512, 1024. Batch sizes: 1 and 4. Hardware: a100-80gb (primary) and g4dn for a lower-cost comparison. We need raw logs and the exact seed/commit so results are reproducible. Short method blurb (1-2 sentences) is great.

sam: Got it. I'll do smoke (single run per combo) tonight on a100 and g4dn, full sweep (multiple runs and stats) Friday. Can you confirm the sample payloads? Do you want the marketing prompt set or anonymized real-world queries?

maria: Use anonymized user queries (I uploaded a scrubbed CSV to the marketing drive), but include a synthetic uniform token distribution run for latency normalization.

sam: Perfect. Here's the smoke command I'll run (also putting this in the runbook):

```
python infra/bench/run_bench.py
  --model open-model-1
  --variant fp16
  --batch 1
  --seq 512
  --runs 50
  --seed 2026
  --hw a100-80gb
  --payloads s3://redwood-marketing/scrubbed_prompts.csv
  --emit-raw-logs s3://redwood-marketing/bench-raw/1829991111/
```

sam: Outputs I'll provide: summary CSV (p50/p95/mean), per-run token counts, raw logs tarball, the git commit hash + diff, and the exact CLI used. Will also attach a 2-sentence method blurb you can copy.

lee: Quick ask from PMM — can marketing use these numbers in the launch post and claim “measured on A100” etc? We may need legal/opt-in.

sam: Yes you can use them as long as you include the hardware and run conditions. Add a note: "results averaged over N runs; median p95 reported; see run artifacts for raw data." I'll draft the line.

alex: Scheduling note — please add the full-sweep job to eng-runtime backlog with priority = high for Friday. I'll make a ticket.

bench-bot: job 1829991111-smoke created by sam; status: queued on a100 farm. ETA: ~2h

maria: Amazing, thanks team. Two last asks: 1) can you include a tiny reproducibility snippet we can paste in the deck (one-liner to re-run smoke)? 2) please export the CSV with additional columns: model_variant, hw, batch, seq, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_sec, cost_per_1M_tokens.

sam: Yep — one-liner will be: `python infra/bench/run_bench.py --model open-model-1 --variant fp16 --batch 1 --seq 512 --runs 50 --seed 2026 --hw a100-80gb --payloads <path>`. CSV columns added. I'll post artifacts and the 2-sentence blurb here when smoke completes.

bench-bot: job 1829991111-smoke started on a100-80gb node-12

sam: Smoke is done — attaching quick summary: open-model-1 fp16 @ a100 (seq512 batch1): p50 32ms, p95 89ms, tokens/sec 1200. open-model-1-quant int8 @ a100 (seq512 batch1): p50 28ms, p95 95ms, tokens/sec 1250. Raw logs at s3://redwood-marketing/bench-raw/1829991111/; commit: ab12cd34ef; seed: 2026. Full sweep queued for Fri.

maria: This is great. Can you also add a short note about variability (warmup, network jitter) for the deck?

sam: Added: "Measurements are median over N runs after a warmup phase; variability may occur across instance types and due to network/IO — see raw artifacts for per-run data."

lee: Perfect. Marketing will draft the launch slide and ping for any copy changes. Thanks Sam :tada:

maria: Thank you!! :raised_hands:
